title: Your phone as a listening partner

bigIdea.text: The app can only help if it hears you clearly. In 5 minutes we check the microphone, the room and your headphones.

proper.text: Analysis works best with the phone's own microphone or wired headphones with a mic, in a quiet room, at your normal reciting volume.
Bluetooth headphones (like AirPods) add a delay of a fifth of a second or more, and some switch the microphone to a low-quality mode while recording. Use wired headphones or the speaker for checks.
Your recordings stay on this phone. Nothing is uploaded unless you share it yourself.

memoryHook.text: Quiet room, wired or speaker, normal voice.

questions.q: Which setup gives the app the clearest recording for checks?
options: Phone speaker or wired headphones in a quiet room
Bluetooth earbuds in a busy café
Holding the phone far away while music plays
Covering the microphone with your hand
explain: Right: a quiet room and a direct microphone give clean audio.
Bluetooth adds delay and noise makes checks unreliable.
Distance and music bury your voice.
A covered mic muffles the sound.

questions.q: Why does the app warn you about Bluetooth headphones?
options: They add delay and can lower microphone quality
They stop the app working offline
explain: Right: the delay spoils timing feedback and the headset mic is lower quality.

questions.q: Where are your practice recordings kept?
options: Only on this phone, unless you share them
explain: Right: they stay on the device.
The public repository never holds recordings.
Nothing is sent to audio hosts.

questions.q: The level check says 'too quiet'. What should you do first?
options: Come closer or recite a little louder
Shout as loud as you can
explain: Right: a normal, closer voice fixes most quiet takes.
Shouting can clip and strain your voice.
One small change usually fixes it.

remnote: Best recording setup for Tilawa Coach checks == Phone speaker or wired headphones, quiet room, normal voice
Why avoid Bluetooth for checks == Big delay and a lower-quality headset microphone
taskNow: Press Allow microphone, measure the room noise, then record 3 seconds of 'Bismillah' and play it back.
